messages:
sam: Quick recap from today's small-batcher + prefetch roll: we launched a 3% canary and the initial telemetry looks solid. :tada:
lei: 24h replay on mixed-prod: median down ~13%, p95 down ~11%, p99 down ~19%. Token compute cost approx -10%. Biggest wins on conversational.quick-reply and short-multi-turn routes.
ops-bot: Canary artifact: https://internal.redwood/bench/2912345678
```
shard-mean:
- baseline p50 26ms -> canary p50 22.6ms (-13%)
- baseline p95 138ms -> canary p95 122.8ms (-11%)
- baseline p99 410ms -> canary p99 332ms (-19%)
- cost/1k tokens: $0.076 -> $0.068 (-10%)
- 5xx rate: 0.09% -> 0.095% (no signal)
```
rahul: We added a short-prefix microcache TTL bump and tuned the small-batcher flush threshold which increased packing density. Observed ~9% higher prefix hit-rate and ~8% fewer fragmentation events.
tara: Rollback triggers we set: p99 relative increase >12% OR error-rate absolute increase >0.5% OR sustained gpu_mem_growth_mb >50 OR coalescer_queue_tail_ms >60. Canary will auto-ramp 3 -> 30 -> 100 over 2.5h if healthy.
sam: Product blurb suggestion: "Runtime tuning reduced median response times by ~13% and tail latency by ~19% for short chat flows; estimated token cost savings ~10%."
lei: I'll upload a seq-length heatmap and a brief note on the fallback policy to the artifact. Monitoring hooks bound to runtime.prefetch.*, runtime.batcher.small.*, gpu.memory.delta. PagerDuty on for 90m.
rahul: FYI we pinned seq>64 to stable kernels during the ramp to limit tail risk. If green at +90m we'll proceed with the planned ramp. Thanks team! :rocket:
